exposure: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) guidelines implementation
cohort: The study participants were 62 women undergoing elective cesarean sections in a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found that 80% of ERAS components could be applied to 71% of patients, with resource limitations as primary barriers, and fitness-for-discharge on day two was associated with early breastfeeding and prevention of intraoperative hypotension.
country: N/A (study performed in a low middle-income country)
cross-section timing: Data was collected during the perioperative period for elective cesarean sections and up to day two post-surgery.
